name: mprotect
synopsis: int mprotect(void *addr, size_t len, int prot);
int pkey_mprotect(void *addr, size_t len, int prot, int pkey);
description: mprotect() changes the access protections for the calling process's memory pages in the specified address range. The address must be aligned to a page boundary. If access violates the protections, the kernel generates a SIGSEGV signal for the process.

parameters.name: addr
parameters.description: Starting address of the memory region to protect, must be aligned to a page boundary

parameters.name: len
parameters.description: Length of the memory region in bytes

parameters.name: prot
parameters.description: Bitwise OR of protection flags such as PROT_READ, PROT_WRITE, PROT_EXEC, PROT_NONE, PROT_SEM, PROT_SAO, PROT_GROWSUP, or PROT_GROWSDOWN

parameters.name: pkey
parameters.description: Protection key for pkey_mprotect(), must be allocated with pkey_alloc(2)

return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error, and errno is set

errors.description: The memory cannot be given the specified access, e.g., trying to make a read-only file writable
addr is not a valid pointer or not a multiple of the system page size
pkey has not been allocated with pkey_alloc(2) for pkey_mprotect()
Both PROT_GROWSUP and PROT_GROWSDOWN were specified in prot
PROT_SAO was specified but SAO hardware feature is not available (PowerPC)
Internal kernel structures could not be allocated
Addresses in the range are invalid or specify unmapped pages
Changing protection would exceed the maximum number of mappings with distinct attributes

versions: mprotect: POSIX.1-2001, SVr4; pkey_mprotect: Linux 4.9, glibc 2.27
